newsitem.title: FRANCE: EMU members must share stability culture - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: EMU members must share stability culture - Tietmeyer.

text.p: Europe would risk a brutal reversal in its move towards greater integration if the future members of economic and monetary union do not agree to share a culture of stability, Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said.

In an interview with afternoon daily Le Monde, he said a budget stability pact to be launched after monetary union to prevent countries running up big budget deficits was important to ensure that all countries shared this stability culture.
"For a long time to come, we will have to live in Europe without a common political will, an element which has however accompanied the launch of any single currency.
"We will continue to live in national states. That is why it is so important to have the same culture of stability," he said.
Monetary union must be a success, but it must also be accepted by everybody in all its political implications.
"Without that, there would be a very brutal reversal in European integration," he said.
Tietmeyer also said there should be no illusions that the new euro would help to create jobs without the structural reforms needed to Europe's labour markets.
"On the contrary, the euro will increase competition between countries and markets and abolish the exchange rate tool, which could be used up to now as an 'airbag'," he said.
